text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A36, A37, A42, A43 and A44 each ran in every trace (participation 100 in 100, about one occurrence per trace); in the later window each appears in only about 55 in 100 traces. A27 fell from every trace to about 46 in 100, while A15, A16, A25, A26, A28 and A31 still appear in every trace in both windows. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL007, REL019, REL025, REL031, REL032]
- Routing into the block changed: before, practically all of A25's outgoing transitions (about 99 in 100) went to one of the five block activities, split roughly 17–24 in 100 each; in the later window about 99 in 100 go to A28 instead. [DIR003]
- Routing out of the block changed: before, each block activity also led to A28 in roughly 17–25 in 100 of its outgoing transitions; in the later window that edge is gone and each leads to A31 in about 14–25 in 100. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010]
- A26's routing changed: before, about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions led to A27; in the later window about 45 in 100 lead to A27 and about 54 in 100 lead to the block activities. [DIR004]
- The block swapped sides relative to A26 and A28: before, it preceded A26 in about 97–98 in 100 traces and preceded A28 in about 97–98 in 100; in the later window A26 precedes the block in about 54–55 in 100 and A28 precedes it in about 54–55 in 100. [REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL038, REL039, REL040, REL041, REL042]
- A27 and the block became alternatives: before, A27 co-occurred with each block activity in every trace, usually after it; in the later window they share a trace in at most about 1 in 100 cases, with A27 alone in about 45 in 100 and the block alone in about 55 in 100. [REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037]
- Mean event positions shifted consistently: A26 earlier (0.62 to 0.53 of the trace) and A28 earlier (0.49 to 0.38), the five block activities later (about 0.41 to 0.58); these are event positions, not clock times. [POS004, POS006, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS012]
- Proximity flipped the same way: before, A25 was within five steps of each block activity in nearly every trace (about 197–200 of 200) and A26 in only 1–2; in the later window this is reversed (about 1–2 versus about 107–108), though one side of each of these comparisons rests on very few observations. [LAG005, LAG007, LAG010, LAG013]
- Separately, A10 now occurs in about 13 in 100 traces instead of about 32 in 100, and its outgoing transitions redistributed, the share going to A16 dropping from about 79 to 38 in 100. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural reorganisation around the block A36, A37, A42, A43, A44: in the earlier window the block ran in every case between A25 and A28, followed by A26, A27 and A31; in the later window A25 bypasses the block and leads almost always directly to A28, while the block reappears after A26 in about 55 in 100 cases as an alternative to A27 — the two almost never occur in the same trace — and the block then flows into A31, which A27 still reaches on its own branch (about 99 in 100 of A27's transitions in both windows). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, REL026, REL031, REL033, REL038, REL043, OCC002, OCC007]

This is shown directly by relational and successor evidence rather than inferred from frequencies alone: A25's successor set changed from the five block activities to A28, A26 gained the block as successors alongside A27, the order between the block and A26/A28 reversed, and A27 and the block switched from always co-occurring to being mutually exclusive; the participation drops and position shifts agree with this reading. With 106 qualifying items against roughly 1.2 expected if nothing had changed, the pattern as a whole is far beyond what random re-splits of stable behaviour produce. [DIR003, DIR004, REL026, REL030, REL033, REL037, REL038, REL042, OCC003, POS004, POS008, POS012]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a genuine relocation of the block from dropping it after A25 and adding a new optional branch after A26, nor can it show whether the block's appearance in about 55 in 100 later traces reflects one routing choice; the LAG agreement rests on only about 1–2 observations per window for most pairs, and the block's internal order remains mixed in both windows, so no internal reordering is claimed. [LAG005, LAG010, REL048, REL055]

Other differences: A10 occurs in about 13 in 100 traces in the later window versus about 32 in 100 earlier, with its outgoing transitions redistributed (share to A16 from about 79 to 38 in 100, and immediate A10→A16 successions weakening); A15, A16 and A25 sit slightly later and A31 slightly earlier in the trace, all small shifts. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS007]
